summary: Security patch bump of next 15.5.23 -> 15.5.24 (with @next/env and @next/swc-*) in the `security` catalog, and the `next` override raised from `next@<15.5.18: ~15.5.18` to `next@<15.5.24: ~15.5.24`. Only pnpm-workspace.yaml and pnpm-lock.yaml change. In this repo `next` is a devDependency of @cipherstash/nextjs (whose published peer range `^14 || ^15` is unchanged and which tsup externalises as a peer) and an optional peer of evlog (a runtime dependency of @cipherstash/stack); workspace overrides and the lockfile are not published, so no shipped artefact's contents or declared ranges change. The realistic failure is a patch-level behaviour change in next/server or next/headers breaking @cipherstash/nextjs's build/tests, which would be loud and was covered by CI: the Node 22/24 test jobs (which run `turbo test` over packages/**) and ci-required passed on the head commit. No material release risk found.

behaviour_changes.description: Workspace `security` catalog pins next to 15.5.24 instead of 15.5.23; lockfile resolves next, @next/env and all eight @next/swc-* platform binaries at 15.5.24 for the packages/nextjs devDependency, the @clerk/nextjs peer and evlog's optional peer.

pnpm override for next raised so any next resolving below 15.5.24 (including 14.x) is forced to ~15.5.24 inside this workspace; pnpm also rewrites the recorded peer ranges of @clerk/nextjs and evlog in the lockfile (~15.5.18 -> ~15.5.24). Workspace-only; overrides are not part of any published package.json.

affected_components.name: pnpm workspace dependency config (pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml)
affected_components.how: Catalog entry and override edited; lockfile regenerated.

affected_components.name: @cipherstash/nextjs (packages/nextjs)
affected_components.how: Declares next and @clerk/nextjs as `catalog:security` devDependencies and imports next/server and next/headers; builds and tests now run against next 15.5.24. Published peer range `^14 || ^15` unchanged.

affected_components.name: @cipherstash/stack via evlog
affected_components.how: Depends on evlog 1.11.0, whose optional peer next is resolved to 15.5.24 in the lockfile. Consumers resolve evlog's peer themselves; the workspace pin does not ship.

affected_components.name: CI install (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile) in all pnpm jobs
affected_components.how: Every pnpm job installs from the lockfile; a lockfile/workspace mismatch would fail install.

failure_scenarios.title: next 15.5.24 patch changes next/server or next/headers behaviour used by @cipherstash/nextjs
failure_scenarios.trigger: The upstream security fix in next 15.5.24 alters NextResponse, NextRequest or cookies() semantics that packages/nextjs relies on.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/nextjs imports NextResponse/NextRequest from next/server and cookies from next/headers (src/index.ts, src/clerk/index.ts); its dev/test resolution moves to 15.5.24. tsup externalises next (peer dependency), so the published dist is not changed by the bump itself.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Local/CI build or test failures for @cipherstash/nextjs; customers are unaffected because they bring their own next within `^14 || ^15`.
